amendment_log.change: The management representation AND its regularisation strength are now selected jointly by train out-of-fold quadratic-weighted kappa. Selected: raw DermLIP features, C=100.0, train OOF QWK 0.5899, margin 0.0718 over the runner-up.
amendment_log.reason: Schema 1 selected the representation by QWK but C by classification accuracy. That incoherence produced two different 'raw-feature probe' management figures from the same representation and split -- 0.6550 (C=10, chosen by out-of-fold log-loss with temperature scaling, in perception_baseline.json) and 0.4648 (C=100, chosen by accuracy). QWK is the registered P2 statistic, so both choices now use it.

amendment_log.change: The management benchmark previously quoted as QWK 0.6550 is withdrawn as the reference value for P2.
amendment_log.reason: That figure came from a probe tuned for calibration (log-loss + temperature), not for the registered endpoint. Under a QWK-consistent selection on train it is not the chosen configuration: raw features at C=10 score 0.4793 train OOF QWK against 0.5899 for C=100. Carrying 0.6550 forward as the benchmark would have compared a QWK-selected model against a differently-selected one.

amendment_log.change: Melanoma under-management is elevated from a secondary note to an endpoint reported with equal prominence to QWK within P2. The registered SELECTION criterion remains QWK, unchanged.
amendment_log.reason: The two endpoints rank the candidate models in OPPOSITE directions on development: meta-features scored QWK 0.3846 with 5/61 melanomas under-managed (8.2%), while the QWK-selected raw-feature arm scores 0.4648 with 8/61 (13.1%). QWK is symmetric and penalises over- and under-treatment equally; under-managing a melanoma is not symmetric with over-managing a naevus. Changing the selection criterion to the safety endpoint AFTER observing this would be fitting the criterion to the result, which is precisely the failure v1 recorded as its v5-to-v6 problem. The criterion therefore stands as registered and the disagreement is published.
amendment_log.future_work_not_adopted_now: A harm-weighted ordinal loss is the defensible selection criterion for a clinical decision endpoint. Adopting it here would be post-hoc; it belongs in a future protocol registered before its data are seen.

amendment_log.change: Adds decision-level endpoints from the evidence layer, all architectural (reported as counts, never hypothesis-tested): withheld rate, conflict rate, escalation rate, undecidable rate, guideline citation rate, and the coverage denominator.
amendment_log.reason: The evidence layer did not exist at schema 1. These describe how the system behaves as decision support rather than as a classifier, and a clinical reader needs them. They are architectural by construction -- an arm without a contract cannot score on them -- so they are barred from hypothesis tests under the same rule v1 used.

amendment_log.change: Records that criterion-level abstention is implemented and tested but currently unreachable.
amendment_log.reason: The INDETERMINATE path yields a score range and keeps a case decidable when unknowns cannot change the verdict. Nothing emits it: the criterion heads always return an argmax, and G1 established that VLM self-reported confidence carries no usable signal (separation 0.0281). Observed undecidable rate on valid is therefore 0.0000. Adding a producer -- for example a posterior-margin threshold -- is a system change and is NOT made here. The capability is reported as present-but-inactive rather than claimed.

relationship_to_v1: Independent study. v1 (medguard-derm-evidence-contract-h2h-v1) is complete and sealed; none of its results are reused as evidence here, only its metric and governance code.
registration_statement: Every configuration choice below -- feature view, base and meta hyperparameters, and the operating threshold -- was selected on the Derm7pt TRAIN split by cross-validation and confirmed once on VALID. This document fixes the system and the analysis before the test split is scored for the proposed system. The test split is NOT pristine: see test_split_exposure.

test_split_exposure.what_was_read: research/evidence/derm7pt_v1/perception_baseline.json contains 395 per-case TEST predictions and test-split metrics for the diagnosis-classifier and management-probe baselines (diagnosis accuracy 0.7392, balanced accuracy 0.5702, macro-F1 0.5940, ECE 0.0455; management accuracy 0.7595, balanced accuracy 0.6888, macro-F1 0.7013, ECE 0.0419).
test_split_exposure.how_it_happened: The baseline characterisation was instructed to report per-split metrics including test, on the reasoning that a baseline is not a system claim. That reasoning was wrong in one specific way: the classifier-alone arm is P1's registered comparator, so its test performance was visible before the ensemble was designed.
what_was_NOT_read: any melanoma-specific sensitivity, specificity or AUROC on test at any threshold

consequence_for_claims.system_performance: The registered system has never been run on test. Its own test performance is genuinely out-of-sample and may be reported as confirmatory.
consequence_for_claims.comparative_performance: The comparator's test metrics were visible during design. The 'stacked beats classifier-alone' comparison is therefore WEAKER than a fully blinded one and must be reported with this disclosure attached. It must not be described as a blinded head-to-head.
consequence_for_claims.mitigation_actually_available: None retroactively. The exposure is recorded rather than repaired.

test_split_exposure.required_for_an_unqualified_comparative_: A confirmatory run on a cohort no part of this project has read -- PAD-UFES-20 or an ISIC held-out partition. Until then the Derm7pt test result is a strong out-of-sample result for the system and a disclosed-exposure result for the comparison.
test_split_exposure.precedent: v1 handled BCN20000 the same way: registered as exposed external-development, never described as untouched confirmation.

thesis: In dermoscopy, combining differently-trained readers of the same image -- a diagnosis classifier and seven per-criterion heads whose outputs are aggregated by the published 7-point rule -- detects melanoma better than either reader alone or than a hand-written combination of them, while preserving an auditable per-criterion rationale.
novelty_boundary: The 7-point checklist, linear probes, stacking and frozen CLIP-family encoders are all established. None is claimed as novel.

The claims are: (a) that criterion heads and a diagnosis classifier built on identical frozen features are empirically complementary, and (b) that a fitted ensemble over them beats a hand-written union rule at a train-fixed operating point.
No claim is made that this system beats specialised dermoscopy classifiers on raw accuracy.
No claim of clinical utility, clinician-perceived quality, or deployability.

scope.dataset: Derm7pt (Kawahara et al.), local copy at release_v0/
scope.unit_of_analysis: case (one lesion per case; no within-case clustering)

splits.source: the dataset's official index files, frozen in research/evidence/derm7pt_v1/manifest.json

test_split_composition_declared_in_advan.note: Composition only, taken from the frozen manifest. No outcome, prediction or score has been computed on these cases.

excluded: multi-view stacking (rejected on train; see rejected_on_train)
criterion localisation claims (Derm7pt ships no segmentation masks)

base_layer.predictions_feeding_meta_layer: out-of-fold on train (5-fold stratified, seed 20260810); full-train refit for evaluation cohorts

meta_layer.composition: per-view diagnosis posterior, seven criterion posteriors, the derived 7-point score, and one-hot patient metadata (sex, location, elevation)
meta_layer.excluded_feature_reason: expert annotation, unavailable at inference; used only to stratify reporting

aggregation.validation: reproduces the gold seven_point_score on 1011/1011 cases
aggregation.note: No model computes the score. INDETERMINATE criteria yield a score range; a case stays decidable when unknowns cannot change the verdict.

operating_point.policy: fixed on train out-of-fold meta-predictions, applied unchanged to any evaluation cohort
operating_point.primary_rule: lowest score at which train out-of-fold sensitivity reaches a pre-declared 0.70
operating_point.note: Both thresholds are fixed. Neither may be re-derived using test data.

endpoints.classification_rule: architectural = guaranteed by construction, reported as counts and never hypothesis-tested; inferential = defined for every arm and not architecturally determined; supporting = reported context.
endpoints.multiplicity: Holm across the three primary endpoints at alpha 0.05, then Holm within each family.

primary.statistic: AUROC for melanoma-vs-rest, stacked ensemble versus the diagnosis-classifier-alone arm
primary.success_condition: AUROC difference favours the stacked ensemble with a 95% interval excluding zero

primary.statistic: quadratic-weighted kappa against gold management, registered arm versus a metadata-only control
primary.selection: representation and C chosen jointly by train out-of-fold QWK; see amendment A1

co_reported_safety_endpoint.name: melanoma under-management rate
co_reported_safety_endpoint.definition: a case whose true diagnosis is melanoma receiving a recommendation below excision
co_reported_safety_endpoint.prominence: reported with equal prominence to QWK; see amendment A3

primary.endpoint_disagreement_disclosed_in_advan: QWK and the safety endpoint rank the candidate arms in opposite directions on development. The QWK-selected arm is the WORSE of the two on melanoma under-management (13.1% versus 8.2%). Both are reported; neither is suppressed.
primary.success_condition: QWK interval excludes zero and exceeds the metadata-only control
primary.known_risk: The train-to-valid QWK gap is large (0.5899 to 0.4648). P2 is the weakest of the three primary endpoints and may not confirm.

primary.statistic: macro accuracy across the seven criteria versus a per-criterion train-majority chance baseline; macro Cohen kappa reported alongside
primary.success_condition: macro accuracy lift over chance with a 95% interval excluding zero

supporting: derived 7-point score MAE, exact-match and within-one rates against gold
diagnosis 5-class confusion matrix, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, MCC, Cohen kappa
calibration (ECE) and risk-coverage (AURC) for the registered arms
all primary endpoints stratified by level_of_diagnostic_difficulty
subgroup reporting by sex, body location and elevation
reader-agreement rate between the diagnosis classifier and the criteria path
architectural_reported_never_tested: the 7-point rule reproducing the gold score on determinate input
the fraction of cases decidable under partial information
withheld rate (contracts failing their own verification obligations)
conflict rate and escalation rate between the two views
guideline citation rate, always with its coverage denominator

decision_level_development_values_valid_.note: Citation rate follows the classifier's COMMITTED condition; the eligible denominator follows the true condition. The gap reflects the system under-calling malignancy, not a retrieval failure.

statistics.clustering: none; each Derm7pt case is one lesion and the case is the unit of analysis
statistics.code: medguard_v2/eval/statistics.py (byte-identical port of the v1 module, parity-tested)

failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.statement: A vision-language model can judge the seven dermoscopic criteria from the image.
failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.evidence: G1: qwen3-vl-32b over the full valid split, macro accuracy 0.5672 against a 0.6256 chance baseline (lift -0.0584). G1c: six configurations including gemini-3.1-pro, claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6-terra, grok-4.5, qwen3-vl-235b, and a visual few-shot condition; none exceeded the chance baseline, best lift -0.0059. Visual few-shot made performance worse.
failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.consequence: No VLM criterion reader appears in the registered system. No further VLM criterion runs will be performed on test.

failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.statement: Assessor self-reported confidence can drive criterion-level abstention.
failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.evidence: G1 confidence separation between correct and wrong answers 0.0281; indeterminate used on 0.98 percent of judgements.
failed_hypotheses_recorded_before_the_co.consequence: Criterion-level abstention is not claimed. Reader-agreement rate is reported as a supporting signal only.

rejected_on_train.statement: Adding DermLIP-clinical, BiomedCLIP-dermoscopic and BiomedCLIP-clinical views improves the ensemble.
rejected_on_train.evidence: All 15 view subsets ranked by train out-of-fold AUROC. Single dermoscopic DermLIP view best at 0.8765; performance declines monotonically with each added view to 0.8635 for all four.
rejected_on_train.interpretation: A sample-size result at n=413, not a claim that these views are uninformative. The feature sets remain cached for a larger-cohort retest.

development_results.repin_reason: G6 was re-run when the management selection criterion was aligned to QWK. The melanoma result is unchanged (AUROC 0.8852); only the management block differs.

confirmatory_run_protocol: Build a v2 runtime lock over medguard_v2 and verify it clean.

Confirm the exposure boundary still holds: perception_baseline.json is the ONLY artifact containing test-split outputs, and it contains no stacked-ensemble, criterion-head or melanoma-threshold result. A test enforces this.
Refit the base and meta layers on train ONLY, using the registered hyperparameters. Do not re-select anything.
Re-verify the runtime lock before scoring.
Record the result in the ledger whether it confirms or refutes.
stop_conditions: any hyperparameter, view, threshold or endpoint is re-selected after test data is read
the test split is scored more than once
an arm is added to the comparison after test outcomes are seen
an architectural endpoint is presented as a hypothesis test
a development number is reported as confirmatory
results are reported for a subset of endpoints chosen after seeing them
invalid_post_test_actions: changing the operating threshold to improve a test number
re-running the confirmatory scoring as a repair
substituting the stacked management arm for the registered raw-feature arm after seeing test results
reporting the multi-view configuration if it happens to score better on test
introducing a VLM criterion reader after the fact
known_limitations_registered_in_advance: Derm7pt is single-centre with 1011 cases; the test split has 101 melanomas.
The diagnosis classifier and criterion heads share one frozen encoder; their complementarity arises from differing training targets, not independent information sources.
Nine cases have no distinct clinical view; they are recorded in the manifest and are irrelevant to the registered single-view system.
The valid split is melanoma-enriched (30.0 percent) relative to train (21.8) and test (25.6); prevalence-dependent statistics do not transfer between splits.
No clinician has evaluated any output.
No segmentation masks exist, so no criterion localisation claim is made.
The management arm was chosen on development data after the stacked variant regressed; this is disclosed rather than concealed.
change_control: Any substantive change requires a new schema version with a written reason. This document is never silently edited after the confirmatory run.
